Chinese Vice President Han Zheng on Monday attended the China-Türkiye Green Development Business Forum in Istanbul together with Turkish Vice President Cevdet Yilmaz, calling for deeper cooperation between the two countries in green development and trade.
In his speech, Han said that China-Türkiye relations have maintained sound and steady development under the strategic guidance of the two countries' heads of state, noting that Türkiye is an important economic and trade partner of China in West Asia and an important partner in Belt and Road cooperation.
China is willing to work with Türkiye to fully implement the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, continuously deepen practical cooperation in various fields, and promote the development of the China-Türkiye strategic cooperative relationship to a higher level, Han said.
The Chinese vice president put forward three proposals for deepening green economic and trade cooperation between the two countries.
First, the two sides should strengthen alignment between their green development strategies. China is unwavering in promoting a comprehensive green transformation of its economic and social development and in pursuing modernization featuring harmony between humanity and nature. China appreciates Türkiye's 2053 net-zero emissions target and is willing to enhance exchanges of ideas and experience with Türkiye, jointly pursuing a sustainable development path characterized by resource conservation, environmental protection, and green and low-carbon growth.
Second, the two sides should advance cooperation in green technologies and industries. China has the world's most complete new energy industrial chain, with mature technologies and comprehensive supporting industries in areas such as solar photovoltaics, wind power and energy storage. These industries are highly complementary to Türkiye's needs for energy transition and development.
China encourages and supports enterprises from both countries in deepening industrial and technological cooperation and pursuing localized production, so as to facilitate the implementation of more high-quality green projects, enhance the competitiveness of Türkiye's new energy industry, and achieve mutually beneficial and win-win outcomes at a higher level, according to Han.
Third, the two sides should deepen multilateral cooperation. China and Türkiye share similar positions on global climate governance. China appreciates Türkiye's important contributions to advancing global climate governance as the country holding the presidency of the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference and is willing to work with Türkiye to promote positive outcomes at the conference.
Han said China stands ready to work with Türkiye to take the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries as an opportunity to deepen exchanges and cooperation in the green sector, share opportunities arising from the green and low-carbon transition, and work together to build a clean, beautiful and sustainable world.
He also called on business communities from both countries to make full use of the forum to deepen exchanges, build consensus and work together to promote further progress in China-Türkiye economic and trade cooperation.
Yilmaz said in his remarks that the global economy is undergoing a major transformation, with the green transition being a key part of the process. China holds an important position in areas of green development, including green technologies, renewable energy and electric vehicles, and has made positive contributions to the global green transition.
Türkiye is actively advancing its 2053 net-zero emissions target and looks forward to deepening practical cooperation with China in areas such as new energy, energy storage systems, smart manufacturing and sustainable infrastructure, working together to achieve sustainable development, Yilmaz said.
Prior to the forum, Han held talks with Yilmaz. Han said China and Türkiye share broad common interests in achieving their respective development goals and upholding international fairness and justice. The two sides should earnestly implement the important consensus reached by their heads of state, support each other's core concerns, strengthen development strategy alignment and deepen mutually beneficial and win-win cooperation, Han added.
China is willing to encourage more Chinese enterprises to invest and establish businesses in Türkiye, and welcomes Türkiye to make good use of platforms such as the China International Import Expo to bring more high-quality Turkish products to the Chinese market, he said. Han also expressed hope that Türkiye would provide a sound and stable business environment for Chinese enterprises, so as to promote the steady and sustained development of China-Türkiye cooperation.
Yilmaz said this year marks the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between Türkiye and China. Last year, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Chinese President Xi Jinping met on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Summit in Tianjin, providing new guidance for bilateral relations, he noted.
China is Türkiye's largest trading partner, Yilmaz stressed, adding that Türkiye looks forward to working with China to make good use of mechanisms such as the China-Türkiye Intergovernmental Cooperation Committee, continuously expand bilateral trade, broaden cooperation in areas including finance, energy, minerals, artificial intelligence and tourism, and promote the alignment between the Middle Corridor initiative and high-quality Belt and Road cooperation.
Türkiye enjoys geographical and human resource advantages and welcomes more Chinese enterprises to invest in the country to achieve mutual benefit and win-win results, according to Yilmaz.
The China-Türkiye Green Development Business Forum was jointly organized by the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade and the Foreign Economic Relations Board of Türkiye. Nearly 300 representatives from the political and business communities of the two countries attended the event.

articles.title: From horseback classrooms to digital lessons: A school transforms lives in Xinjiang
articles.titleCn: 从马背课堂到数字课堂：新疆一所学校改变人生
articles.summary: Decades ago, a teacher in a remote pastureland in northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region rode from one herding camp to another, carrying a small blackboard and a few textbooks on horseback.
articles.summaryCn: 新疆偏远牧区的一所学校从教师骑马流动教学发展为拥有数字屏幕、校车和寄宿设施的现代化学校，几代人的教育条件发生了翻天覆地的变化。

paragraphs.en: (ECNS) -- Decades ago, a teacher in a {{0}} {{1}} in northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region rode from one herding camp to another, carrying a small blackboard and a few textbooks on horseback. A copper bell hanging from his saddle {{2}} his arrival. Wherever herders pitched their tents, he would set up a classroom, and children would gather for lessons. Today, students in the same mountain valley travel to school by bus and take lessons on digital screens. At Beitashan Pasture Primary School, located in Beitashan Pasture in the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps' Sixth Division near China's border with Mongolia, the {{3}} of education has {{4}} over generations.
paragraphs.cn: （中新社）——几十年前，在中国西北部新疆维吾尔自治区的一片偏远牧场上，一位教师骑着马从一个牧民营地到另一个牧民营地，马背上驮着一块小黑板和几本教科书。挂在他马鞍上的铜铃宣告着他的到来。无论牧民在哪里搭起帐篷，他就在那里设立课堂，孩子们便聚集起来上课。如今，同一片山谷里的学生们乘公交车上学，在数字屏幕上听课。位于新疆生产建设兵团第六师北塔山牧场、靠近中国与蒙古边境的北塔山牧场小学，教育的变革历经几代人逐步展开。

paragraphs.en: The school is the only one in the area, which lies on the eastern edge of the Junggar Basin. With an average {{5}} of more than 3,000 meters and strong winds on nearly 300 days a year, the remote pastureland {{6}} challenges for both daily life and education. "Things have changed a lot over the years," said Hu Rimanhan Abudukeba, a retired teacher at the school, now 79. As a child, Hu followed his family's sheep across different pastures. His teacher, Xia Lifu Khan Tulekebai, traveled on horseback, carrying a small blackboard and textbooks, with a copper bell hanging from his saddle.
paragraphs.cn: 这所学校是该地区唯一的一所学校，位于准噶尔盆地东缘。这里平均海拔超过3000米，一年近300天刮大风，偏远的牧场给日常生活和教育都带来了挑战。“这些年来变化很大，”该校退休教师胡热曼汗·阿布德克巴现年79岁，他说道。小时候，胡热曼汗跟着家里的羊群辗转于不同的牧场。他的老师夏力甫汗·吐勒克巴骑着马，带着一块小黑板和教科书，马鞍上挂着一只铜铃。

paragraphs.en:
The teacher moved from one herding site to another, holding classes wherever families had settled. When children heard the bell, they knew their teacher had arrived. The mobile teaching arrangement came to be known locally as the "school on horseback."
In the autumn of 1955, the pastureland got its first {{7}} school. A wall coated with black paint served as a blackboard, while a {{8}} desk consisted of a wooden plank resting on several wooden supports. Hu learned to write there under Xia's {{9}}.
paragraphs.cn: 老师从一个放牧点走到另一个放牧点，在牧民家庭安顿下来的地方就地开课。孩子们听到铃声，就知道老师来了。这种流动教学方式在当地被称为“马背学校”。1955年秋天，牧场有了第一所固定学校。一堵涂了黑漆的墙充当黑板，一张临时课桌由一块木板架在几根木支架上搭成。胡热曼汗在夏力甫汗的指导下在那里学会了写字。

paragraphs.en: With the education he received, Hu later went from being a shepherd boy to becoming a teacher at the same school. The journey to school looks very different for today's pupils. (ECNS) -- Decades ago, a teacher in a remote pastureland in northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region rode from one herding camp to another, carrying a small blackboard and a few textbooks on horseback.
A copper bell hanging from his saddle announced his arrival. Wherever herders pitched their tents, he would set up a classroom, and children would gather for lessons.
Today, students in the same mountain valley travel to school by bus and take lessons on digital screens.
At Beitashan Pasture Primary School, located in Beitashan Pasture in the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps' Sixth Division near China's border with Mongolia, the transformation of education has unfolded over generations.
The school is the only one in the area, which lies on the eastern edge of the Junggar Basin. With an average altitude of more than 3,000 meters and strong winds on nearly 300 days a year, the remote pastureland presents challenges for both daily life and education.
"Things have changed a lot over the years," said Hu Rimanhan Abudukeba, a retired teacher at the school, now 79.
As a child, Hu followed his family's sheep across different pastures. His teacher, Xia Lifu Khan Tulekebai, traveled on horseback, carrying a small blackboard and textbooks, with a copper bell hanging from his saddle.
The teacher moved from one herding site to another, holding classes wherever families had settled. When children heard the bell, they knew their teacher had arrived. The mobile teaching arrangement came to be known locally as the "school on horseback."
In the autumn of 1955, the pastureland got its first permanent school. A wall coated with black paint served as a blackboard, while a makeshift desk consisted of a wooden plank resting on several wooden supports. Hu learned to write there under Xia's guidance.
With the education he received, Hu later went from being a shepherd boy to becoming a teacher at the same school.
The journey to school looks very different for today's pupils.
One recent morning, sixth-grader Aysulu Serikbay, who lives in Caojianlian, a pastoral area, put on her backpack and boarded a school bus.
The bus takes students home free of charge every Friday and brings them back to school after the weekend.
"I really like the school bus. It has air conditioning in summer and heating in winter, so it's very comfortable," she said.
Her father, Serikbay Nurahamat, works in border patrol and attended the same school as a child. Back then, his family lived more than 30 kilometers from the school. He and his friends had to walk the distance together, a journey that took considerable time.
After starting his own family, he moved to Caojianlian. Now, his daughter can simply take a school bus to get to class, a change that gives him peace of mind.
Inside the classroom, the differences are just as striking.
During a Chinese language lesson, teacher Liu Zhao switched on an interactive display, showing students an animated presentation of the text. The class then read a classical Chinese poem together, with Liu slowing down his speech and guiding the children through each line.
In the same mountain valley where a teacher once carried a blackboard on horseback, lessons are now delivered through digital screens.
The school also provides boarding facilities and meals for students whose families live far away. Under a government meal subsidy program for boarding students, each pupil pays 545 yuan per semester for meals.
"The school is wonderful. It has beautiful teaching buildings and dormitories, as well as a running track. My dad is quite envious of me," Aysulu said.
She sometimes brings Liu a traditional dairy snack called nanguru (milk curds) made by her mother.
"I especially like Teacher Liu's Chinese lessons. He often tells us about the beautiful landscapes across China. I hope to get into a junior high school in Xinjiang and go beyond the mountains to see a bigger world," she said.
Liu is also the school's principal. He moved there last year from a primary school in Wujiaqu, a city in Xinjiang. Every two weeks, he makes a 400-kilometer drive to return home.
But he said the children's parents face even greater challenges.
More than 70 percent of the pupils have family members engaged in border patrol work, according to the school. These family members spend about 10 days each month stationed in the mountains, unable to return home. Many children have lived at the school since first grade.
"Their parents are up in the mountains guarding the border and can only come home for a few days each month. Once the children are entrusted to us, we have to take good care of them," Liu said.

Meanwhile, Europe is seeking a role in the negotiations as the talks get underway in Abu Dhabi. However, an expert says the talks are unlikely to yield substantial progress, given the wide gaps between the parties' positions and priorities.
Leadership reactions to the progress of the meeting
Following the first day of trilateral meetings, the leaders of Ukraine and the US special envoys have both called the talks "constructive," while Russian officials remain cautious about giving an assessment of the progress.
Zelenskyy said the talks were "constructive and quite substantive," adding that they covered humanitarian and security issues.
Speaking to reporters later in Denmark, Zelenskyy said he was pleased with messages he had been receiving from the two US presidential envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.
"I see changes. I am very happy about what I hear," Zelenskyy said.
"The release of prisoners (of war) is a priority. They spoke in detail about the substance of security guarantees for Ukraine and the foundations for ensuring these guarantees function over the long term," he posted on X.
Kushner wrote on X after the first day wrapped up that he was "encouraged by the constructive discussions today."
He said the US side was working to end the war and "establish the security arrangements necessary for a sovereign, secure, and prosperous Ukraine and lasting peace across Europe."
Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov struck a more cautious note, saying it was too early to assess the meeting ahead of a second day of talks on Wednesday.
Europe seeks greater involvement
Meanwhile, Europe is seeking a greater role in the peace negotiations, which could reshape the region's security framework.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on Monday that the European Union (EU) would be present while the Kremlin said the core negotiations would involve Russia, Ukraine and the United States. The exact format of European participation remained unclear.
Euronews reported on Monday that concerns were growing in European capitals that decisions on the continent's security could be made without their involvement.

Assessing the prospects for the peace talks, Su Xiaohui, director of the Department for Developing Countries Studies at the China Institute of International Studies, said the results of the US midterm election has added uncertainty to the outlook.
Su said the Republican Party's setbacks in the midterm elections have left the US administration eager to shift domestic attention away from the Iran issue and the stalemate between Washington and Tehran.
The administration has sought to draw public attention to the prospect of progress in resolving the Russia-Ukraine conflict in the near term, Su observed. However, by reducing the regional conflict to personal differences between the leaders of Russia and Ukraine, the US risks oversimplifying the issue and rushing the process, which will do little to ease the challenges of resolving the crisis down the road, she added.

A Chinese mainland spokesperson said on Wednesday that policy measures will continue to be introduced to deepen economic integration across the Taiwan Strait and to share the mainland's modernization opportunities and benefits with Taiwan compatriots.
Zhang Han, a spokesperson for the State Council's Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks at a regular press conference, noting that the communique of the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China, held at the outset of the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), has been warmly received by Taiwan compatriots and businesspeople.
"Chinese modernization is the common cause of all the sons and daughters of the Chinese nation, and the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation is the long-cherished aspiration of compatriots on both sides of the Taiwan Strait," Zhang said.
She said the mainland will continue to strengthen cross-Strait economic and trade cooperation, deepen integrated development, and promote exchanges and interactions across the Strait.
Zhang noted that as the mainland's economy continues to improve, with structural adjustments speeding up and improving, domestic demand potential being unlocked, and innovation vitality surging, Taiwan businesspeople and enterprises will find greater space for development, more opportunities and better safeguards on the mainland.
In a separate development, Taiwan-based personal computer brands ASUS and Acer have moved part of their production capacity from Thailand and Vietnam back to the Chinese mainland, a move that has drawn attention across the island and renewed focus on the deep integration of cross-Strait industrial and supply chains.
Commenting on the shift, Zhang said the mainland has the world's most comprehensive industrial system and a mature and well-developed supporting industrial network, making it the best choice for Taiwan-funded manufacturers to invest and grow.
"The close and resilient cross-Strait industrial and supply chains not only benefit the growth of Taiwan enterprises and the well-being of compatriots on both sides, but also contribute to the security, stability and smooth operation of global industrial chains," she said.
Zhang added that the blueprint of the 15th Five-Year Plan has now been laid out, with high-level opening up and in-depth reform working in tandem to release stronger momentum and provide robust support for Taiwan enterprises to achieve faster and better development amid industrial transformation.
"We will, as always, support Taiwan businesspeople and enterprises in seizing opportunities, investing and doing business on the mainland, and participating in the high-quality development of the mainland economy to achieve better and faster growth," she said.

articles.fullText:
China has built the world's largest and fastest-growing renewable energy system, according to a report released on Saturday by the China Enterprise Reform and Development Society (CERDS).
The report found that fossil fuel-related activities remain the largest source of global carbon emissions. Global energy-related CO2 emissions rose 0.4% year on year to 38.4 billion tonnes in 2025, marking the smallest annual increase since 2021. China's energy-related carbon emissions fell by 0.5%, while those of the United States rose by 2.4%, making the US the largest contributor to the global increase.
A view of a large-scale solar power base in the desert in north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, September 14, 2025. 
Coal-fired power generation accounted for 49.7% of China's total electricity generation in the first half of 2026, falling below 50% for the first time. According to Peng Huagang, president of CERDS, coal power is gradually shifting from a dominant source of electricity to a supporting source that ensures power supply security and provides flexibility to the grid.
Wind turbines and solar panels at a renewable energy base in Karamay, northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, October 10, 2025. 
By the end of 2025, global installed renewable energy capacity had reached 5,149 gigawatts, up 15.5% year on year. Renewables accounted for 33.8% of global electricity generation, surpassing coal's 33.0% share for the first time in a century. In China, installed renewable energy capacity stood at 2.337 billion kilowatts at the end of 2025, accounting for 60.1% of the country's total installed power generation capacity. China also contributed 63.6% of global additions to renewable energy capacity.
A cargo ship is docked to load large wind power equipment for export to Türkiye in Lianyungang, east China's Jiangsu Province, October 21, 2026. 
China's energy investment is projected to reach $940 billion in 2026, the highest in the world.
The report also highlighted China's leading role in renewable energy technologies. China supplies 70% of the world's wind power equipment and 80% of its solar photovoltaic (PV) modules, helping drive down global wind and solar power generation costs by more than 60% and 80%, respectively.
